skill.name: container-orchestration
skill.description: Provides practical Docker, Docker Compose, Kubernetes, Helm, and AWS ECS/Fargate patterns for building, deploying, and operating containerized applications.
skill.summary: Create and review container images, local stacks, Kubernetes resources, Helm charts, and ECS/Fargate configurations.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown formatting, fixed test commands, localhost health checks, and normal container configuration. Confirmed risks include weak database credentials, plaintext production secret examples, and an exposed debug listener. The Compose template also publishes unauthenticated Redis.

remediation.issue: Runnable Compose examples use a predictable PostgreSQL password and publish the database port.
remediation.suggestion: Require DB_PASSWORD without a fallback, avoid publishing the database port, or bind it only to 127.0.0.1 for local use.

remediation.issue: Production Kubernetes examples embed database and API credentials in Secret stringData.
remediation.suggestion: Remove literal credentials and use ExternalSecret references, sealed secrets, or clearly marked placeholders that cannot be deployed unchanged.

remediation.issue: The Compose template publishes Redis without authentication.
remediation.suggestion: Do not publish Redis by default. When host access is required, bind to 127.0.0.1 and configure Redis authentication.

remediation.issue: The debug container listens on all interfaces without access controls.
remediation.suggestion: Bind debugpy to localhost, require a protected tunnel, and warn users never to publish the debug port in shared environments.

content.value_statement: Container deployments require consistent image, networking, configuration, and runtime decisions. This skill provides reusable patterns for Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, and ECS/Fargate.
actual_capabilities: Creates multi-stage Dockerfile patterns with non-root users, health checks, and production stages.
Drafts Docker Compose stacks with application, PostgreSQL, Redis, volume, and network configuration.
Provides Kubernetes Deployment, Service, Ingress, ConfigMap, Secret, NetworkPolicy, and CronJob patterns.
Guides Helm chart structure, values, dependencies, and reusable templates.
Explains ECS/Fargate task definitions, services, networking, load balancing, secrets, and scaling.
Builds and optionally pushes Docker images through a configurable shell script with dry-run support.
limitations: Generated configurations require review for application ports, resources, credentials, and cloud account settings.
The skill does not provision clusters, cloud accounts, registries, or networking infrastructure by itself.
The included build script requires Docker and performs a registry push only when explicitly requested.
Examples do not replace organization-specific security, reliability, cost, or compliance controls.

use_cases.title: Package an application
use_cases.description: Create a production Dockerfile and local Compose stack for a service with database and cache dependencies.

use_cases.title: Deploy to Kubernetes
use_cases.description: Draft workload, service, ingress, configuration, secret reference, resource, and health probe manifests.

use_cases.title: Choose a managed runtime
use_cases.description: Compare ECS/Fargate and Kubernetes against operational complexity, scaling, networking, portability, and team experience.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Dockerfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production Dockerfile for [application]. Use [runtime version], a non-root user, dependency caching, and health endpoint [path].

prompt_templates.title: Build a local stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Docker Compose setup for [service], [database], and [cache]. Use environment placeholders, health checks, named volumes, and internal networks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Kubernetes resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Kubernetes resources for [application]. Include deployment strategy, probes, resources, service, ingress, configuration, external secret references, and network policy.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate orchestration platforms
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare ECS/Fargate and Kubernetes for [workload]. Evaluate scaling, networking, security, cost, portability, operations, and migration risk. Recommend an implementation plan.

output_examples.input: Create a production container plan for a Python API with PostgreSQL and Redis.
output: A multi-stage Python image runs as a non-root user and exposes health and readiness endpoints.
The local stack keeps data services on an internal network and loads credentials from external configuration.
The deployment plan defines resource limits, rolling updates, persistent data, and service health checks.

output_examples.input: Should a small AWS team deploy this stateless API on ECS/Fargate or Kubernetes?
output_examples.output: Recommendation: use ECS/Fargate when AWS integration and low operational overhead outweigh portability needs. Reassess Kubernetes when workload diversity or platform requirements grow.

best_practices: Pin image versions and scan base images and dependencies before release.
Run containers as non-root and apply minimal filesystem, network, and IAM permissions.
Store credentials in managed secret systems and keep literal values out of manifests and images.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy example credentials, default passwords, or plaintext Secret values.
Do not expose databases, caches, or remote debuggers on all host interfaces.
Do not run generated deployment commands before reviewing the target cluster, account, namespace, and registry.

faq.question: Does this skill execute deployments automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and a Docker build script. Cluster and cloud deployment still require explicit commands and credentials.

faq.question: Which container platforms are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers Docker, Docker Compose, Kubernetes, Helm, and AWS ECS on Fargate.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready manifests?
faq.answer: It generates strong starting points, but every manifest needs review for security, resources, networking, availability, and organization standards.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use managed secret stores, External Secrets, sealed secrets, or runtime injection. Never commit real credential values.

faq.question: Does the build script push images by default?
faq.answer: No. Pushing requires the explicit push option. Use dry-run to inspect the resolved build plan without invoking Docker.

faq.question: When should ECS/Fargate be preferred over Kubernetes?
faq.answer: Prefer ECS/Fargate for AWS-focused workloads needing lower platform overhead. Prefer Kubernetes when portability, ecosystem breadth, or advanced scheduling is essential.
